key_insight: Infrastructure as Code can rapidly deploy governed, hospital-controlled AI services for clinical use through a browser or API.
clinical_relevance: This approach may make it easier for hospitals to deliver privacy-compliant AI tools to clinicians without installing workstation software.
method: Encoded secure backend, private AI endpoint, and identity/access setup as machine-readable infrastructure files.
Deployed a hospital-governed LLM service accessible from a browser or API.
Built an inconsistency checker to flag contradictory statements in clinical documents.
evidence_signal: Deployment took 310.3 ± 196.6 seconds on average (n=25), and the inconsistency checker flagged severe inconsistencies in 105 of 1,347 physician-approved documents; 149 of 150 sampled findings were confirmed (population-weighted PPV 98.2%).
watch_item: Results come from a single tertiary-care case study, so broader generalizability and integration burden may vary across institutions.
paper_title: Introducing Infrastructure as Code for deployment and governance of medical AI: A case study
